I never understand why people poo on these devices, they perform just fine imo. Are they going to beat more expensive NVRs, obviously not, but it would likely do 90% of what a normal person would want cams for.
[Floppyflynn] @jigna27: agreed, its such a steal aswell for $12 i dont think id be able to find better
[netsurfer] @jigna27: They don't perform just fine. These Outdoor ones, especially without subscription, are subpar.
You tend to need to use a setting which preserve batteries (and that means even higher chance to miss events).
Battery life isn't good enough if you put these in high traffic area.
Doesn't seem to have low battery life notification (or very inconsistent) so you only notice them when the camera is offline.
Often, one of the 2 batteries goes flat first. If you just replace one, then the other one will be next. If you replace both, you go through lithium AA batteries more quickly (and they aren't cheap).
Sync Module 2, if you have subscription (or on trial), the local storage becomes inconsistent (since cloud storage is used).
And I am being kind. I do use Blink cameras, but as secondary. Tired of needing to place them in either low traffic area or turn off motion events (so manually watch the cameras when needed). They are cheap, but you get what you paid for.
[otto1989] @netsurfer: What you're saying matches a few YouTube reviews.
I think for $20/$12 these cameras, as you say, are pretty darn good as secondary, low traffic, budget cameras that you'd not want to pay subscription for.
I've got the Eufy eco system (which I've been mostly happy with), and got these blink cameras just to place in "nice to have, low traffic" zones (I.e. pretty much FOMO purchased…)
